Resolves #18047

🌿 *The multi-window half of the native titlebar path now has a witness, so wherever the Neural Link battery runs on a display that can stage it, "popup onto popup was never exercised" is unsayable.*

One Neural Link e2e spec, `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL.spec.mjs`, sibling of the main-window arm from #18029: two panes pop out through the real header action, the main window shrinks, the target vessel is placed fully on-screen below it, and the source vessel is moved by "titlebar" (CDP window bounds as the window-server stand-in, zero pointer events, zero runtime patching) straight onto the target and nudged twice inside the dwell window. The spec asserts the production receipts in order: the claim names the target vessel, the target popup renders the drop preview while the main window renders none, the park receipt is `parked`, `transferItem` commits into the target vessel's tabs, the source vessel retires, the target document holds both panes and the exact live pane instance is visible in the target popup. The measurement that motivated it, and the four rig facts the spec header records, are on Epic #15239 ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15239#issuecomment-5500682844)).

Evidence: L3 (Playwright e2e on a real 800×600 display, CDP `Browser.setWindowBounds` as the physical-window adapter; a real OS titlebar drag is not reproducible in Playwright) → L3 required (AC-1…AC-5). Residual: AC-1 (a battery run at or after the merged head, since the Neural Link tier is runtime-gated out of CI), Residual-Owner: #17844.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | Spec at the named path; 3 consecutive local runs green at the PR head on this host's 800×600 display; `test.skip` fires with the display size in its reason when the stage is smaller than 760×560. |
| AC-2 | Assertions, in order: `claimTrace.at(-1)` matches `{claimedStableId: 'workstation-vessel:metrics', outcome: 'claimed'}`; `.neo-dock-preview-affordance` count in the target popup > 0 with 0 in the main window; `lastVesselParkReceipt.parked === true`; `lastCrossWindowTransfer` `{operation: 'transferItem', targetWorkspaceId: 'workstation-vessel:metrics', applied: true}`; `tearOutPanes.commits` null and the source popup closed. |
| AC-3 | No `page.mouse`, no CDP `Input.*`, no `dispatchEvent`, no `publishGeometry()` in the spec; a `mouseout` counter installed in the source realm before any movement is asserted at 0 right after the last move — before the preview and dwell polls, so the read cannot race the source vessel's retirement and carries no catch (round-1 action). |
| AC-4 | `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` and `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` are not in the diff; the former is 1/1 green at this head on this host (see Test Evidence), the latter skips here (stage too narrow) exactly as on `dev`. |
| AC-5 | Spec header lists the four rig facts (emulated screen vs `viewport: null`, Chrome's minimum main-window width, pop-outs before the shrink, arbiter seniority). |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive. The spec uses `metrics` as the target and `commits` as the source exactly as the ticket prescribes; the target lands below the main window because Chrome refuses a main window narrow enough to leave room beside it.

## Test Evidence
- New spec: 3 consecutive runs, all green (7.5s / 7.3s / 7.2s), `dev@c5aa0d2c11` + this spec. Not in CI (the Neural Link tier is runtime-gated); #17844 owns battery runs.
- Sibling `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL`: 1/1 green (6.0s) at this head (unchanged file, same runtime root).
- Trigger discipline receipt: the source realm's `mouseout` counter read 0 in every run; the arm reads previews only after the second geometry update, per the async measurement.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: **`:353` can report a clean gesture without having measured one, and this is the spec where that is most reachable.**

```js
expect(await source.popup.evaluate(() => globalThis.__nativeTitlebarMouseouts).catch(() => 0),
    'no mouseout reached the source realm during the gesture').toBe(0);
```

If that `evaluate` rejects — the source realm gone, navigated, or torn down — the catch substitutes `0`, which is the passing value. The assertion's failure mode and its success mode produce the same reading.

Three things make this worth an action rather than a note:

1. **The merged sibling makes the identical read with no catch.** `origin/dev` `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL.spec.mjs:255`: `expect(await popup.evaluate(() => globalThis.__nativeTitlebarMouseouts), 'no mouseout reached the popup realm during the gesture').toBe(0);` So this is a deviation from the established pattern, not the house style.
2. **It is the only `.catch(() =>` in the file.** One catch, on the AC-3 assertion.
3. **The swallowed state is reachable *here specifically*, and it was not in the sibling.** In the sibling the popup reintegrates and survives the gesture. In this spec the source vessel is *supposed to retire* — the spec asserts `sourceClosed: true` at `:382`. `:353` sits before the retire block, but the terminal is dwell-driven and in flight during the `expect.poll` at `:346`, so the source can retire between the poll settling and the evaluate landing. **The one spec where the measured realm legitimately dies is the one that swallows a failed measurement of it.**

That ordering also suggests the catch was added because the read flaked there, which would make it a race papered over rather than a defensive nicety — worth saying out loud since only you know whether it was.

**The fix is one line, either way.** Drop the catch to match the sibling, or catch into a sentinel that cannot pass (`.catch(() => 'probe-unavailable')` against `.toBe(0)`), so an unmeasurable probe reds instead of greens. The pre-gesture read at `:319` already carries the counter's liveness proof, so nothing else needs to change.
